**Solution 2 (2/5) is refuted.** Its own construction is beaten by the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ circulant in Solution 1. In $D_7$, every vertex has out-degree 2 and in-degree 2, so $\Delta = 4$. Its generators $\{1,3\}$ are disjoint from their negatives $\{6,4\}$, so it is an oriented graph. Its directed triangles come only from step patterns $\{1,3,3\}$, giving the 7 triangles listed in Solution 1. Each vertex lies in exactly 3 of them. Any two vertices cover at most $3+3=6$ triangles, so $fvs(D_7)\ge 3$, and removing $\{0,2,4\}$ leaves only the arc $5\to1$, which is acyclic. Hence $fvs(D_7)/7 = 3/7 > 2/5$, so $c^* \ge 3/7$.

**Solution 3 (1/2)** has a flawed lower bound. A random or Eulerian 4-regular orientation is not shown to force $fvs \ge n/2$, and the "expander" argument is only asserted. Its upper-bound argument also fails at the last step. A max-cut gives induced degree at most 2 in each part, but odd cycles such as triangles have independent sets smaller than half their size, so $n/2$ does not follow. Its answer is unsupported, though not disproven by anything I checked.

**Solution 1 (3/7)** has a verified lower bound. Its upper bound $fvs \le 3n/7$ is not actually proved: the reduction argument is only sketched, and the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ construction being the extremal case is asserted rather than shown. I could not verify the exact supremum independently, but 3/7 is the only candidate here that survives the checks I could make, and it is consistent with a clean extremal construction.

CHOICE: 1
